chunks: (3) And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni informed us, from some of his men, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Huraysh, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, from his fathers, that the Commander of the Faithful said:

"Indeed, the Night of Predestination is in every year, and in that night the affair of the year and what is decreed therein descends. And for this affair there are guardians after the Messenger of Allah." Ibn Abbas asked, "Who are they, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "I and eleven from my loins, inspired Imams."
ai.seo_question: Who are the guardians of the annual divine decrees according to Imam Ali (as)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the theological link between Laylat al-Qadr and the annual revelation of divine decrees (*amr al-sana*), assigning the authority to interpret and implement these decrees to the Twelve Imams. By identifying the Imams as *muḥaddathūn* (those divinely inspired or conversing with angels), it underscores their unique role as the living guardians of the year's spiritual and temporal affairs, a concept central to Shia eschatology and the doctrine of occultation.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (3) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob al-Kulayni narrated from some of his companions from Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Khalid al-Barqi from al-Hasan bin al-Abbas bin al-Huraysh from Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ali al-Baqir (as) from his fathers (as) that Amirul Mo’mineen (as) had said to ibn Abbas: “The Night of Predestination comes every year. In this night all that concerns the year and that will occur is revealed. This matter has guardians after the Prophet (S).”
Ibn Abbas asked, “O Amirul Mo’mineen, who are they?” He said: “I and eleven ones of my progeny; divinely inspired imams.”
